html:
SMTO-POL-0029 — SMTO couldn't ask for permission to use these items

GUID: 2e19da7d-ebbc-57f8-90cd-067177f90700
Slug: resource-reference-invalid
Domain: POL · Subsystem: resource-access

What happened

  • SMTO tried to ask for your permission, but its list of items was empty, too long, or included something it hadn't looked up in this task. No permission question was shown and nothing was allowed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a moment and watch the conversation. SMTO usually looks the items up again by itself and then shows a permission card. The list was only out of date or the wrong size, which SMTO can usually correct on its own.
  2. If it stops or repeats the problem, send a message asking SMTO to look up the items again and ask about no more than 16 at once. SMTO can only ask about items it found in this task, and at most 16 in one question.
  3. Tell SMTO exactly which files, computers or services you want it to use. A precise request helps SMTO find the right items instead of naming ones it never looked up.

What success looks like

  • A permission card appears listing the items, or SMTO says it already has access and carries on.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't approve access to anything you didn't ask for just to get past this; SMTO finding an item doesn't mean it may use it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • request_resource_access was rejected because it named zero or more than sixteen distinct resource references, or a reference that is not among this task's current discovery candidates.

What this means

  • The request contains zero or more than sixteen distinct references, or at least one reference is absent from this task's discovery candidates. Validation stops before a permission question is created. A candidate may have been evicted; this result does not establish that the underlying resource was deleted.

Why this can happen

  • The request contains zero or more than sixteen distinct references, or at least one reference is absent from this task's discovery candidates. Validation stops before a permission question is created. A candidate may have been evicted; this result does not establish that the underlying resource was deleted.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the requested references with the current task discovery results and count distinct references.

How to fix it

  • Call discover_resources again in the same task and pass one to sixteen distinct resource_refs from its current results to request_resource_access. A missing candidate may have been evicted from the discovery list; this rejection does not establish that the underlying resource was deleted.
  • Discover the intended resources again and submit one to sixteen of the returned references.

Retry and execution caution

  • Retry only the permission request after refreshing and correcting its references.

How to verify the fix

  • The refreshed request either displays its permission question or reports that access is already granted.

What not to do

  • Do not invent resource references or treat discovery as permission to use a resource.

Technical notes

  • No new permission question or grant is committed by this rejection.
  • The resource may still exist; candidate validity does not establish resource existence or prior execution.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
